title: Delaney Hall: Third Detainee Death; Edwin Lopez-Cornejo Dies After Medical Emergency
excerpt: Edwin Lopez-Cornejo, a 41-year-old Salvadoran detainee held at New Jersey's Delaney Hall facility, died at University Hospital in Newark on August 1, 2026 — the third detainee death connected to the facility. His family said he was denied daily medication for diabetes and high blood pressure.
content:
On August 1, 2026, Edwin Lopez-Cornejo, a 41-year-old citizen of El Salvador, died at University Hospital in Newark, New Jersey, after suffering a medical emergency while detained at Delaney Hall, a private immigration detention center operated by the GEO Group.

  • Lopez-Cornejo's mother said he was not receiving daily medication for diabetes and high blood pressure, and that he had complained of numbness in his face and hand in their final conversation.
  • Lopez-Cornejo's death was the third connected to Delaney Hall since the facility reopened in May 2025, though ICE did not count all deaths in its official tallies after its June 2026 policy change eliminating post-release death reporting.
  • Newark Mayor Ras Baraka called the death "a heartbreaking reminder of the consequences of a facility that has operated for far too long without adequate oversight, accountability, or transparency."
  • A congressional letter described "contaminated food, extreme temperatures, overcrowding and one detainee with an active case of tuberculosis" at the facility.

ICE defended the facility, saying Lopez-Cornejo "received proper medical care and was seen by medical professionals." Congressional Democrats and advocacy groups disputed this account and demanded independent investigation.
